newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria targets growth at 5.5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria targets growth at 5.5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Nigeria's military government is targetting 1997 growth in Gross Domestic Product at 5.5 percent versus 3.25 percent in 1996, the finance minister said on Monday.

"It is anticipated that policy, programmes and strategies especially those bordering on stimulating non-oil activities will result in an improved growth rate," said Anthony Ani in his breakdown of the 1997 budget.

Military ruler General Sani Abacha on Saturday announced an annual budget which put off the question of privatisation, widely hoped for by business and international lending agencies, until after further study.
Ani named privatisation and liberalisation of power generation, telecommunications and oil and gas as being among strategies to be adopted for growth.
"Government will carefully manage the privatisation exercise to ensure that the country obtains its maximum profits," he said.
Other strategies which were given prominence in his speech include stimulating agriculture and food production, family economic development and development of solid minerals.
"The proper implementation of the policies and programmes of this year's budget will go a long way in strengthening the structure of the economy and raising the level of production," Ani said.
